exercises.title: Bài 1 · Admitting a new patient
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Mr Tran, aged 68, arrives at the hospital with chest tightness. At the reception desk, a nurse checks his ID and puts an ID wristband on his arm. She asks him to sit down and says, "Could you tell me what the problem is?" Mr Tran explains that he has felt pain in his chest since the morning.

In the triage area, the nurse takes his blood pressure and asks about his medical history. Mr Tran says that he has diabetes and that he is allergic to penicillin. The nurse writes both facts on his chart and puts a red allergy label on it. She also asks for the name of his next of kin. His daughter, Hoa, is his emergency contact, and the nurse calls her at once.

Because his symptoms may be serious, Mr Tran is admitted to the cardiology ward. Before he is taken there, the nurse explains the plan: "The doctors will do some tests, and I will stay with you until the porter arrives. Is that all right?" Mr Tran nods and says that he feels safer already.

content.q: Mr Tran has had chest pain since the evening.
content.why: Đoạn 1: anh ấy đau ngực **since the morning**.

content.q: Mr Tran is allergic to penicillin.
The nurse calls Mr Tran's daughter.
content.why: Đoạn 2: Hoa là người liên lạc khẩn cấp và được gọi ngay.

content.q: Mr Tran is sent home after triage.
content.why: Đoạn 3: ông được **nhập khoa tim mạch**.

content.q: What does the nurse put on Mr Tran's arm?
Who is Mr Tran's emergency contact?
Why is Mr Tran admitted to the cardiology ward?
content.why: Đoạn 3: triệu chứng có thể nghiêm trọng.

content.q: What does the nurse do before he goes to the ward?
content.why: Đoạn 3: nữ điều dưỡng giải thích kế hoạch.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Talking to a worried patient
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Ms Pham speaks little English, so the nurse, Anna, asks an interpreter to join them. Anna explains that she would like to ask a few questions, and she promises that everything will stay confidential.

"Would you mind telling me what brought you here today?" Anna asks. Ms Pham says that she has had a bad cough for three weeks and that she feels tired all the time. Anna asks how often she coughs at night and whether she has a fever. Ms Pham coughs mostly at night, and she does not know if she has a fever, because she has no thermometer at home.

After the interview, Anna says, "I'll take your temperature now. Could you open your mouth, please?" The temperature is 38.4°C. Anna tells Ms Pham that the doctor will see her soon and offers her a glass of water. Before she leaves, she asks, "Is there anything else that worries you?" Ms Pham smiles and answers that she understands everything now. Good bedside manner, Anna says later, is mostly about listening.

content.q: Ms Pham speaks fluent English.
content.why: Đoạn 1: bà nói **little English**, nên cần phiên dịch.

content.q: Anna promises that the conversation will be confidential.
Ms Pham has had a cough for three weeks.
content.why: Đoạn 2: 'a bad cough for three weeks'.

content.q: Ms Pham's temperature is normal.
content.why: Đoạn 3: nhiệt độ **38.4°C**, cao hơn bình thường.

content.q: Why does Anna ask an interpreter to join them?
content.why: Đoạn 1: Ms Pham nói ít tiếng Anh.

content.q: When does Ms Pham cough most?
Why does Ms Pham not know if she has a fever?
content.why: Đoạn 2: bà không có nhiệt kế ở nhà.
opts: She has no thermometer at home

content.q: What does Anna say good bedside manner is mostly about?

exercises.title: Bài 1 · How patients describe pain
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
When patients describe pain, nurses listen for several details. First, the location: does it hurt in the chest, in the abdomen or in a joint? Second, the type of pain. Patients often say that the pain is sharp, dull, burning or throbbing. These words give the care team important clues.

Next, the nurse asks how long the symptoms have lasted. A patient who has had a fever for three days needs different care from someone who has had one since this morning. The nurse also asks whether anything makes the pain better or worse, for example movement, food or rest. Finally, she uses a pain scale from 0 to 10, where 0 means no pain and 10 means the worst pain imaginable.

Some symptoms are urgent. Chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden numbness on one side of the body and heavy bleeding need immediate attention. In these cases, the nurse must call a doctor at once.

content.q: The nurse asks only about the location of the pain.
content.why: Đoạn 1–2: còn hỏi **loại đau**, **thời gian**, yếu tố làm đau nặng/nhẹ hơn.

content.q: The pain scale goes from 0 to 10.
Chest pain is an urgent symptom.
content.why: Đoạn 3: đau ngực cần chú ý ngay.

content.q: In urgent cases, the nurse should wait before calling a doctor.
content.why: Đoạn 3: cô ấy **must call a doctor at once**.

content.q: Which type of pain is mentioned in the text?
What does 10 mean on the pain scale?
content.why: Đoạn 2: 10 = cơn đau tồi tệ nhất có thể tưởng tượng.

content.q: Why does the nurse ask how long the symptoms have lasted?
content.why: Đoạn 2: thời gian khác nhau cần cách chăm sóc khác nhau.
opts: To fill in the insurance form

content.q: Which symptom needs immediate attention?
content.why: Đoạn 3: tê đột ngột một bên cơ thể là triệu chứng khẩn cấp.
opts: Sudden numbness on one side of the body

exercises.title: Bài 2 · A patient with abdominal pain
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Last night, Mr Binh, aged 45, came to the emergency department with abdominal pain. He told the nurse that the pain had started two days earlier. At first it was dull, but it has become sharper, and it is now on the lower right side of his abdomen. He has also had nausea since yesterday, and he vomited twice this morning. He has not eaten anything for twenty-four hours.

The nurse measured his temperature, which was 38.1°C, and his pulse, which was 104 beats per minute. She noticed that he was pale and that he felt dizzy when he stood up. She asked whether he had diarrhoea, and he said that he had not. She also asked about his medical history. Mr Binh said that he had never had surgery and that he was not taking any medication.

Because his symptoms were getting worse, the nurse reported them to the doctor immediately. The doctor ordered blood tests and a scan. Mr Binh was told not to eat or drink anything until the doctors had examined him.

content.q: The pain started two days earlier.
content.why: Đoạn 1: cơn đau bắt đầu **two days earlier**.

content.q: Mr Binh has diarrhoea.
content.why: Đoạn 2: ông nói là **không** bị tiêu chảy.

content.q: His temperature was 38.1°C.
Mr Binh has had surgery before.
Where is the pain now?
content.why: Đoạn 1: vùng bụng dưới bên phải.
opts: On the lower right side of the abdomen

content.q: How many times did he vomit this morning?
Why did the nurse report to the doctor immediately?
content.why: Đoạn 3: triệu chứng đang nặng lên.

content.q: What was Mr Binh told?
content.why: Đoạn 3: không ăn uống cho đến khi bác sĩ khám.
opts: Not to eat or drink until he had been examined

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Measuring vital signs
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Vital signs give the nursing team a quick picture of a patient's condition. The four main measurements are temperature, pulse, respiratory rate and blood pressure. Many hospitals also check oxygen saturation, and some use a pain scale.

A normal adult pulse is usually between 60 and 100 beats per minute, and a normal respiratory rate is between 12 and 20 breaths per minute. A healthy adult's temperature is around 37°C, and a reading above 38°C is called a fever. Blood pressure is written as two numbers, for example 120/80. A reading that is much higher than normal may indicate hypertension, and one that is much lower may indicate hypotension.

The nurse must follow a few rules. First, she explains the procedure and asks the patient to sit quietly for a few minutes. Next, she measures carefully, using clean equipment. Finally, she records each result at once on the chart and compares it with the baseline. If a value is abnormal, she should inform the doctor without delay.

content.q: The four main vital signs are temperature, pulse, respiratory rate and blood pressure.
A reading above 38°C is called a fever.
The nurse records the results at the end of the day.
content.why: Đoạn 3: cô ghi kết quả **at once** (ngay lập tức).

content.q: Blood pressure is written as one number.
content.why: Đoạn 2: huyết áp viết bằng **hai số**, ví dụ 120/80.

content.q: What is a normal adult pulse?
content.why: Đoạn 2: mạch người lớn thường 60–100 lần/phút.

content.q: What does the nurse do first?
content.why: Đoạn 3: trước hết giải thích và cho bệnh nhân ngồi yên.
opts: She explains the procedure and asks the patient to sit quietly

content.q: What should the nurse compare each result with?
What should she do if a value is abnormal?

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Checking on Mrs Hanh
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
At 8 a.m., the nurse, Linh, measured Mrs Hanh's vital signs after her operation. Her temperature was 36.8°C, her pulse was 78 beats per minute and her blood pressure was 118/76. Her oxygen saturation was 97%. These readings were all within the normal range.

At 2 p.m., Mrs Hanh said that she felt hot and weak. Linh checked her again. Her temperature had risen to 38.6°C, her pulse was now 112, and her oxygen saturation had fallen to 93%. She was also breathing faster than before. The patient was drowsy, but she answered when Linh spoke to her.

Linh did not wait. She told Mrs Hanh to stay in bed and not to get up alone. Then she called the doctor and gave a clear report: the temperature was higher than in the morning, the pulse was faster, and the oxygen level was lower. The doctor arrived within ten minutes and ordered tests. Linh checked the vital signs every thirty minutes until the patient's condition improved.

content.q: At 8 a.m. all of Mrs Hanh's readings were within the normal range.
Her oxygen saturation rose in the afternoon.
Linh waited until the evening to call the doctor.
Linh measured the vital signs every thirty minutes afterwards.
content.why: Đoạn 3: đo mỗi 30 phút cho đến khi tình trạng cải thiện.

content.q: What was Mrs Hanh's temperature at 2 p.m.?
How did Mrs Hanh feel in the afternoon?
content.why: Đoạn 2: bà thấy nóng và yếu.

content.q: What did Linh tell Mrs Hanh to do?
content.why: Đoạn 3: nằm yên trên giường, không tự ý đứng dậy.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Giving medication safely
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Giving medication is one of a nurse's most important tasks, and mistakes can be dangerous. That is why nurses follow the five rights: the right patient, the right drug, the right dose, the right route and the right time.

Before giving a drug, the nurse reads the prescription carefully and checks the patient's ID wristband. She also asks about allergies and reads the label on the box. If the expiry date has passed, the medicine must not be used. The nurse then prepares the correct dose. Tablets and capsules are given orally, syrups are measured in a small cup, and injections are given with a needle and syringe.

After the patient has taken the drug, the nurse records the time, the dose and the route on the chart. She stays alert for side effects, such as a rash, vomiting or dizziness. If the patient has an allergic reaction, the nurse must stop the medication and call the doctor immediately. Controlled drugs are kept in a locked cabinet, and every dose is counted and signed for.

content.q: The five rights include the right dose and the right route.
The nurse may use medicine after its expiry date.
content.why: Đoạn 2: thuốc hết hạn **must not be used**.

content.q: Controlled drugs are kept in a locked cabinet.
The nurse records the dose before the patient takes the drug.
content.why: Đoạn 3: ghi **sau khi** bệnh nhân đã uống thuốc.

content.q: What does the nurse check on the patient's arm?
content.why: Đoạn 2: kiểm tra vòng tay định danh.

content.q: How are syrups given?
content.why: Đoạn 2: siro được đong bằng cốc nhỏ.
opts: They are measured in a small cup

content.q: What should the nurse do if the patient has an allergic reaction?
content.why: Đoạn 3: dừng thuốc và gọi bác sĩ ngay.
opts: Stop the medication and call the doctor

content.q: What is recorded on the chart?
content.why: Đoạn 3: giờ, liều và đường dùng thuốc.
opts: The time, the dose and the route

exercises.title: Bài 2 · A near miss on the ward
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Last Tuesday, a medication error was almost made on a surgical ward. Nurse Minh was preparing the evening medicines when she noticed that a dose of insulin in the syringe was larger than the one in the doctor's order. The order said 6 units, but 16 units had been drawn up. She stopped immediately.

Minh did not give the injection. Instead, she showed the syringe to a second nurse, who confirmed the mistake. The syringe was thrown away in the sharps bin, and a new dose was prepared and checked by both nurses. The injection was given safely fifteen minutes later, and the patient's blood sugar was monitored.

An incident report was completed before the end of the shift. It explained what had happened: the prescription had been read in a hurry, and the number had been written unclearly. After the incident, the ward introduced a new rule: all insulin doses must be double-checked by two nurses. The manager thanked Minh and said that reporting near misses helps to keep patients safe.

content.q: The patient received the wrong dose.
content.why: Đoạn 2: Minh **did not give** mũi tiêm sai liều.

content.q: A second nurse confirmed the mistake.
content.why: Đoạn 2: y tá thứ hai xác nhận sai sót.

content.q: The syringe was thrown away in the sharps bin.
content.why: Đoạn 2: ống tiêm được bỏ vào **sharps bin**.

content.q: The ward did not change any rules.
content.why: Đoạn 3: khoa **đưa ra quy định mới**.

content.q: What did Minh notice?
content.why: Đoạn 1: liều trong ống tiêm lớn hơn y lệnh.
opts: The dose in the syringe was larger than the order

content.q: Why was the number wrong?
content.why: Đoạn 3: đọc vội và số bị viết không rõ.
opts: The prescription had been read in a hurry and written unclearly

content.q: When was the injection given safely?
What new rule was introduced?
content.why: Đoạn 3: mọi liều insulin phải được hai y tá kiểm tra chéo.
opts: Insulin doses must be double-checked by two nurses

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Preventing infection in hospital
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Hospitals care for people who are sick, and many of them are very weak. For this reason, preventing infection is a priority. Infections can be spread by touch, by the air or by contaminated equipment, and this is called transmission.

The most effective measure is hand hygiene. Nurses must clean their hands before touching a patient, before any aseptic procedure, after touching a patient and after touching the patient's surroundings. If their hands look dirty, they wash them with soap and water. Otherwise, they can use alcohol gel.

Staff also wear personal protective equipment, or PPE, such as gloves, masks and gowns, to protect themselves and the patients. Gloves must be changed between patients; if they are not, cross-infection may occur. Used needles go into a sharps bin, and surfaces are disinfected regularly. Patients with highly infectious illnesses are kept in isolation so that the infection does not spread to others.

content.q: Infections can spread through the air.
content.why: Đoạn 1: lây qua chạm, không khí hoặc dụng cụ nhiễm bẩn.

content.q: Nurses use alcohol gel if their hands look dirty.
content.why: Đoạn 2: tay bẩn thì **rửa bằng xà phòng và nước**.

content.q: Gloves must be changed between patients.
Highly infectious patients are kept in isolation.
What is the most effective measure mentioned?
Where do used needles go?
What can happen if gloves are not changed between patients?
content.why: Đoạn 3: có thể xảy ra lây nhiễm chéo.

content.q: Why are infectious patients kept in isolation?
content.why: Đoạn 3: để bệnh không lây sang người khác.
opts: So that the infection does not spread to others

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Changing a wound dressing
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Nurse Thu has to change a dressing on Mr Long's leg wound. First, she explains the procedure and asks whether he has any pain. If he does, she gives a painkiller about thirty minutes before the procedure, as ordered. Then she washes her hands and puts on a clean apron and gloves.

She removes the old dressing carefully and puts it in a yellow waste bag. Next, she looks at the wound. If it is red, hot or swollen, or if there is a bad smell, she will report it to the doctor. Today the wound looks clean. She cleans it with a sterile swab and saline, moving from the cleanest area outwards. She changes her gloves, dries the skin around the wound and applies a new sterile dressing.

Finally, she disposes of the waste, washes her hands again and writes a note on the chart: the date, the time, the condition of the wound and the type of dressing used. She also tells Mr Long to keep the dressing dry and to call a nurse if it becomes loose.

content.q: Thu puts on gloves before washing her hands.
content.why: Đoạn 1: cô **rửa tay trước**, sau đó mới mang găng.

content.q: The old dressing is put in a waste bag.
content.why: Đoạn 2: bỏ vào túi rác y tế màu vàng.

content.q: The wound looks infected today.
Thu writes a note on the chart.
content.why: Đoạn 3: cô ghi ngày, giờ, tình trạng vết thương và loại băng.

content.q: When does Thu give a painkiller if the patient has pain?
content.why: Đoạn 1: khoảng 30 phút trước thủ thuật.
opts: About thirty minutes before the procedure

content.q: What does Thu use to clean the wound?
content.why: Đoạn 2: gạc vô trùng và nước muối sinh lý.

content.q: In which direction does she clean the wound?
content.why: Đoạn 2: từ vùng sạch nhất ra ngoài.
opts: From the edge towards the dirtiest part

content.q: What does she tell Mr Long?
content.why: Đoạn 3: giữ băng khô và gọi y tá nếu băng bị lỏng.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · A good handover
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A handover is the moment when one nurse gives information about patients to the next nurse at the end of a shift. A poor handover can cause mistakes, so many hospitals teach a simple structure called SBAR.

S stands for Situation: the nurse says who the patient is and what is happening now. B stands for Background: she gives the medical history, such as allergies and recent surgery. A stands for Assessment: she reports the latest vital signs and her own opinion about the patient's condition. R stands for Recommendation: she says what she thinks should be done next, for example: "I think the doctor should see the patient within the hour."

Good handovers are short, accurate and clear. The nurse avoids unusual abbreviations and checks that the other person has understood. Important information is also written in the medical record, because speech can be forgotten, but a legible note stays. If a patient is deteriorating, the nurse must escalate the problem at once and not wait until the next handover.

content.q: A handover happens at the end of a shift.
In SBAR, the letter B stands for Background.
content.why: Đoạn 2: B = Background (bệnh sử, bối cảnh).

content.q: Nurses should use as many unusual abbreviations as possible.
content.why: Đoạn 3: nên **tránh** từ viết tắt hiếm gặp.

content.q: A deteriorating patient should wait until the next handover.
What does the nurse report under Assessment?
content.why: Đoạn 2: dấu hiệu sinh tồn mới nhất và nhận định của cô.
opts: The latest vital signs and her own opinion

content.q: Why is important information also written in the record?
content.why: Đoạn 3: lời nói có thể bị quên, còn ghi chú thì còn lại.
opts: Speech can be forgotten, but a note stays

content.why: Đoạn 2: điều nên làm tiếp theo.
opts: What the nurse thinks should be done next

content.q: What should the nurse do after giving the handover?
content.why: Đoạn 3: kiểm tra người nhận đã hiểu chưa.
opts: Check that the other person has understood

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Reporting an incident
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
On Sunday night, Nurse Quang found Mr Duc sitting on the floor next to his bed. Mr Duc said that he had wanted to go to the toilet and that he had not wanted to disturb anyone. He said that he felt a little pain in his hip, but he insisted that he was fine.

Quang called for help and checked Mr Duc's vital signs. Then she asked him whether he had hit his head. He answered that he had not. A doctor was called and examined him. The doctor told Quang to monitor him every hour and ordered an X-ray.

Before the end of her shift, Quang completed an incident report. She wrote what she had seen, the time, the doctor's name and what the patient had said. She also noted that Mr Duc was a fall risk and that his call bell had been out of reach. In the handover, she told the morning nurse that the patient needed close observation and that the call bell should always be placed within his reach.

content.q: Mr Duc said that he had wanted to go to the toilet.
Mr Duc told Quang that he had hit his head.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Basic life support
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Cardiac arrest is a life-threatening emergency: the heart stops pumping blood, and the patient becomes unconscious and stops breathing normally. Every minute without treatment reduces the chance of survival, so nurses must act immediately.

First, the nurse checks that the area is safe and tries to wake the patient by speaking loudly and touching his shoulders. If there is no response, she calls for help and sends someone to bring the crash cart and the defibrillator. In a hospital, she may call code blue. Then she opens the airway and checks for normal breathing for no more than ten seconds.

If the patient is not breathing normally, she starts CPR at once. She pushes hard and fast in the centre of the chest and continues until the defibrillator arrives or until the team takes over. As soon as the defibrillator is ready, it must be attached and its instructions must be followed. Nobody should stop CPR unless the patient wakes up or a doctor tells them to stop.

content.q: In cardiac arrest, the heart stops pumping blood.
The nurse should check breathing for several minutes.
CPR should continue until the defibrillator arrives or the team takes over.
The nurse should call for help only after finishing CPR.
content.why: Đoạn 2: gọi giúp đỡ **trước** khi bắt đầu CPR nếu bệnh nhân không đáp ứng.

content.q: What does the nurse do first?
content.why: Đoạn 2: kiểm tra an toàn và cố gọi bệnh nhân tỉnh.
opts: She checks that the area is safe and tries to wake the patient

content.q: What equipment is brought to the patient?
content.why: Đoạn 2: xe cấp cứu và máy sốc tim.
opts: The crash cart and the defibrillator

content.q: How long should she check for normal breathing?
When can CPR be stopped?
content.why: Đoạn 3: khi bệnh nhân tỉnh hoặc bác sĩ yêu cầu dừng.
opts: If the patient wakes up or a doctor says so

exercises.title: Bài 2 · A busy night in the emergency department
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
At 11 p.m., an ambulance arrived at the emergency department with a man who had fallen from a motorbike. The paramedics told the triage nurse, Lan, that he was conscious but confused, that he had a bleeding leg and that his breathing was fast.

Lan classified him as a high priority and took him straight to the resuscitation room. While a colleague was attaching a cardiac monitor and an oxygen mask, Lan applied pressure to the wound until the bleeding slowed. His blood pressure was low and his pulse was fast, which showed that he was going into shock. The doctor arrived within two minutes and ordered fluids through a cannula, blood tests and an X-ray.

Within half an hour, the patient's condition was stable. He had a fractured leg and was taken to the operating theatre. Lan then handed over to the surgical team. When she finished, she wrote in the record what she had done, at what time, and what the patient's vital signs had been. "In an emergency," she said later, "staying calm is as important as acting fast."

content.q: The man had fallen from a motorbike.
content.why: Đoạn 1: ông ngã từ xe máy.

content.q: He was unconscious when he arrived.
content.why: Đoạn 1: ông **conscious but confused** (tỉnh nhưng lú lẫn).

content.q: The doctor arrived within two minutes.
content.why: Đoạn 2: bác sĩ đến trong vòng hai phút.

content.q: The man had a fractured leg.
Where did Lan take the patient?
content.why: Đoạn 2: đưa thẳng vào phòng hồi sức.

content.q: What did Lan do to the wound?
content.why: Đoạn 2: ép vào vết thương cho đến khi máu chảy chậm lại.
opts: She applied pressure until the bleeding slowed

content.q: What showed that he was going into shock?
content.why: Đoạn 2: huyết áp thấp và mạch nhanh.
opts: Low blood pressure and a fast pulse

content.q: What did Lan say was as important as acting fast?
content.why: Đoạn 3: giữ bình tĩnh quan trọng ngang với hành động nhanh.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Planning a safe discharge
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Going home from hospital is an important step, and good preparation reduces the risk that a patient will return soon. Discharge planning starts early. Nurses talk to the patient and the family about the patient's needs, the medicines and the help that will be available at home.

Before discharge, the nurse gives clear discharge instructions. She explains how and when to take each medicine, which side effects to expect and which warning signs mean that the patient should call a doctor, for example a high fever, increasing pain or bleeding. She also gives advice about diet, exercise and rest. The nurse uses simple words, avoids long medical terms and asks the patient to repeat the main points. This method is called "teach back."

If the patient needs rehabilitation or a caregiver, the nurse arranges it. A follow-up appointment is made, and the patient receives the phone number of the ward. Finally, the nurse asks, "What questions do you have?" Patients who understand their care are more likely to follow the plan and recover well.

content.q: Discharge planning starts on the day of discharge.
content.why: Đoạn 1: kế hoạch xuất viện **bắt đầu sớm**.

content.q: The nurse explains which warning signs mean the patient should call a doctor.
content.why: Đoạn 2: ví dụ sốt cao, đau tăng, chảy máu.

content.q: The nurse uses long medical terms.
content.why: Đoạn 2: cô dùng từ đơn giản và **tránh** thuật ngữ dài.

content.q: A follow-up appointment is made.
What is "teach back"?
content.why: Đoạn 2: bệnh nhân nhắc lại các ý chính.
opts: The patient repeats the main points

content.q: Which of these is a warning sign?
content.why: Đoạn 2: sốt cao là dấu hiệu cần gọi bác sĩ.

content.q: Why is discharge planning important?
content.why: Đoạn 1: giảm nguy cơ phải quay lại viện.
opts: It reduces the risk that the patient will return soon

content.q: What does the nurse ask at the end?

exercises.title: Bài 2 · An ethical dilemma
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Mrs Mai, aged 82, has a serious illness. Her son asks the nurse, Thao, not to tell his mother about the diagnosis because he is afraid that she will become very sad. Thao listens with empathy and tells him that she understands his worry. However, she explains that patients have the right to information about their own health, and that Mrs Mai must give informed consent before any treatment.

Thao speaks to the doctor, and they decide to meet the family together. In the meeting, the doctor asks Mrs Mai how much she would like to know. Mrs Mai says that she wants to hear everything, because she wants to make her own decisions. The doctor explains the diagnosis slowly and in simple language, and Thao stays beside Mrs Mai during the conversation.

Afterwards, Thao writes in the record what was discussed and what Mrs Mai decided. She also arranges support from the palliative care team. Her son says that he is grateful, because he did not realise that his mother was stronger than he thought. For Thao, the case is a reminder that a nurse is an advocate: she protects the patient's dignity and rights, even when it is difficult.

content.q: Mrs Mai's son wants the nurse to tell his mother everything.
content.why: Đoạn 1: anh muốn nữ điều dưỡng **không** nói về chẩn đoán.

content.q: Patients have the right to information about their own health.
content.why: Đoạn 1: Thao giải thích quyền được biết thông tin.

content.q: Mrs Mai wants to hear everything.
content.why: Đoạn 2: bà muốn nghe tất cả để tự quyết định.

content.q: Thao refuses to listen to the son.
content.why: Đoạn 1: Thao **lắng nghe với sự đồng cảm**.

content.q: Why does the son ask Thao to say nothing?
content.why: Đoạn 1: anh sợ mẹ sẽ rất buồn.
opts: He is afraid his mother will become very sad
He is angry with the doctor
He does not believe the diagnosis

content.q: What does the doctor ask Mrs Mai?
content.why: Đoạn 2: bà muốn biết đến mức nào.
opts: How much she would like to know

content.q: What does Thao arrange afterwards?
content.why: Đoạn 3: hỗ trợ từ nhóm chăm sóc giảm nhẹ.
opts: Support from the palliative care team

content.q: What is a nurse, according to the final sentence?
content.why: Đoạn 3: điều dưỡng là người bênh vực quyền lợi và phẩm giá của bệnh nhân.
opts: A person who decides for the family
An advocate who protects the patient's dignity and rights
